sections.markdown:
## C — New laws and information: motorcycle lane sharing, school bus lights, work zones, DVS conduct, the pre-application and the written and road test checklists
Knowledge domain: the front chapter of the Minnesota manual that collects recent law reminders (motorcycle lane sharing, school bus lights, work zones), the conduct rules at driver's license offices, the online pre-application, and the item-by-item checklists an applicant brings to the written test and the road test.

FACT_ID: sec01-F01 | anchor: A01
In Minnesota a motorcycle may legally ride or pass in the space between your vehicle and a vehicle in the next lane, and you must not get in the way of its safe movement. [A01]
Why it matters: this is listed first among the new laws, so expect it as a true-or-false item.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F02 | anchor: A01
You will most often see motorcycle lane sharing at a stoplight as riders move up to the front, but riders may also pass slow traffic on your left or right while using part of your lane. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F03 | anchor: A01
Flashing red lights on a school bus tell drivers that students are boarding or leaving the bus. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F04 | anchor: A01
When a school bus is stopped with its red lights flashing, you must stop your vehicle no closer than 20 feet from the bus. [A01]
Why it matters: the stopping distance is a classic numeric test item.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F05 | anchor: A01
You must stop for a school bus showing flashing red lights even when its stop arm has not swung out. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F06 | anchor: A01
The one exception to stopping for a school bus with flashing red lights is when you are on a divided highway and traveling in the opposite direction. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F07 | anchor: A01
Failing to stop for a school bus with its red lights flashing can bring fines and a suspension of your driver's license. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F08 | anchor: A01
In a work zone, stay alert for distracted driving, zipper merges and changed lane patterns, because crews work very close to moving traffic and large construction vehicles can move unpredictably. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F09 | anchor: A02
Interfering with or obstructing the work of a Driver and Vehicle Services employee is a crime under Minnesota Statute 609.50, Subdivision 5. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F10 | anchor: A02
Driver and Vehicle Services does not tolerate disruptive behavior or harassment, obscene or abusive language or gestures, interfering with services, refusing staff instructions, or violent conduct; a customer who does any of these is asked to leave and police are called. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F11 | anchor: A02
The pre-application in DVS online services lets you finish a large part of your license application before the visit and lists the documents each license type requires, which shortens your time at the counter. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F12 | anchor: A02
Begin the online pre-application no more than 30 days before your office visit so you do not have to fill out a paper application, and bring the confirmation page together with every document it lists. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F13 | anchor: A03
Driver and Vehicle Services offers a virtual assistant at drive.mn.gov in English, Spanish, Somali and Hmong, and a MyDVS account lets you follow your license and registration information online. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F14 | anchor: A03
The Commissioner's message reminds drivers that driving is a privilege that carries a responsibility to everyone else on the road: buckle up, obey speed laws and never drive under the influence of alcohol. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F15 | anchor: A04
Before the Class D written test you need a scheduled test appointment, and the checklist says to finish the online pre-application at dps.mn.gov/mydvs within the 30 days before that appointment, not earlier. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F16 | anchor: A04
For the written test, bring the required identification and money for the fees, and know your Social Security number if you are eligible to have one. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F17 | anchor: A04
An applicant younger than 18 must be at least 15 years old to take the written test. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F18 | anchor: A04
An applicant under 18 brings either a Blue Card, showing classroom instruction is finished and behind-the-wheel training is scheduled, or a Pink Card, showing enrollment in a concurrent driver education course with the first 15 classroom hours completed. [A04]
Why it matters: the two enrollment cards are easy to mix up.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F19 | anchor: A04
Written test applicants under eighteen must be at least fifteen, bring a Blue Card or Pink Card, bring the Supplemental Parental Curriculum completion certificate if completed, and have an approved adult sign the application with documentation when not a parent [A04].
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F20 | anchor: A04
For the road test you need an appointment, a completed online pre-application, and a licensed driver who comes with you; without that licensed driver the road test may be cancelled. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F21 | anchor: A04
At the road test you hand your valid instruction permit to the examiner. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F22 | anchor: A04
The road test vehicle must be safe: doors open from inside and outside, seat belts work, and the headlights, taillights, brake lights and turn signals all function, with registration that is current or covered by a 60-day permit. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F23 | anchor: A05
Proof of insurance for the road test vehicle can be the original card from the insurance company, the policy declaration page, or electronic proof from the insurer's website or shown on a device. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F24 | anchor: A05
A road test applicant under 18 must be at least 16 years old and bring the White Card showing driver education was completed. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F25 | anchor: A05
A road test applicant under 18 must have held an instruction permit for the past six months with no conviction for a moving violation or for an alcohol or controlled substance violation. [A05]
Why it matters: permit holding time differs by age, so pair this with the adult rules.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F26 | anchor: A05
If some or all of a teen's six months of permit driving took place in another state, the teen brings a certified driving record from that state to show eligibility for the provisional license. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F27 | anchor: A05
A road test applicant under 18 brings a Supervised Driving Log that is filled in and signed by a parent or guardian, plus the parental approval signature on the application. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F28 | anchor: A05
An 18-year-old road test applicant must have held the instruction permit for at least six months, while an applicant aged 19 or older needs at least three months. [A05]
Why it matters: the age split for permit holding time is a common confusable.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0008]

Misconceptions: the stop arm does not decide whether you stop, because flashing red lights alone require it; lane sharing by motorcycles is legal, not a violation to block; the opposite-direction exception applies only on a divided highway; the road test can be cancelled if no licensed driver comes along, even when the applicant is ready.
Mnemonics: Blue Card before the permit test, White Card before the road test, Pink Card for a concurrent course; red lights flashing means stop whether or not the arm is out.
Glossary: DVS means Driver and Vehicle Services, the Department of Public Safety division that licenses drivers; pre-application means the online form started before an office visit; Blue, Pink and White Cards mean the driver education certificates of enrollment and completion; Supervised Driving Log means the parent-signed record of a teen's practice driving.
Dynamic facts: fees, websites, the virtual assistant languages and appointment systems can change; confirm them at drive.mn.gov before a visit.

corpus_stability.reason: The Minnesota Driver’s Manual prints a single edition line (June 2026) on its front cover and opens with a New laws and information chapter that collects recent changes in one place, with no sign of more than one rewrite per year in the selected pages.
